details: Bitcoin (BTC) is trading around $87,000, continuing its upward momentum. This rally is underpinned by easing macroeconomic pressures, including declining bond yields across Asia and falling Brent crude oil prices, which foster a "risk-on" sentiment in global markets. The cryptocurrency has demonstrated resilience, having absorbed a recent Federal Reserve interest rate hike and the failure of the US Senate's "Clarity Act" aimed at digital asset regulation. Markets interpreted the Fed's rate hike as a sign that future tightening may proceed slowly. Analysts are increasingly optimistic, with some suggesting Bitcoin has entered a new bull market regime.
title: Bitcoin Maintains $87,000 Amid Easing Macro Pressures

details: European central banks, including the ECB, are proposing to expand the existing stablecoin interest ban to include crypto lending and staking activities. This move aims to close regulatory loopholes and mitigate systemic risks by replacing fixed reserve requirements with maturity-linked liquidity standards, and by implementing stricter oversight for foreign-currency stablecoins. The recommendations were submitted as part of the European Commission's MiCA review consultation, highlighting ongoing concerns about financial stability and investor protection in the crypto market.
title: EU Central Banks Push for Broader Stablecoin Yield Ban
